paragraphs: Beruriah, daughter of Rabbi Chanina ben Teradyon, wife of Rabbi Meir. She was wise. She is mentioned in a baraita in Tosefta Kelim, chapter 8, and Rabbi Yehoshua said, “Beruriah has spoken well.” It is cited there in Rabbi Shimshon’s commentary, mishnah 4. So too in the Arukh, entry kelastra (see above, Rabbi Chalafta of Kefar Chananya). In Sefer Keritot, Leshon Limmudim, gate 2, section 93: the daughter of Rabbi Chanina ben Teradyon disagrees with her father, and the law follows her words, in Tosefta Kelim, chapter 4. Thus in two places the law follows her. In chapter Tamid Nishchat, 62b: although she learned 300 teachings from 300 rabbis on a winter’s day, nevertheless she had not fulfilled the requirement in three years … to learn Sefer Yuchasin. (The statement “Rabbi Yehoshua said, ‘She has spoken well’” requires examination; I have written about it on a separate sheet.) According to this tradition, she is a reincarnation of Bathsheba, who would teach Solomon and admonish him; likewise she taught students and was seduced by one student (see above, Rabbi Meir). That student was the soul of Uriah: she had been the cause of his death, and now he was the cause of her death (Gilgulei Neshamot). See what I wrote about her story and her end under Rabbi Meir.
